questions.q: What does back-of-the-envelope estimation actually turn Lesson 2's requirements into?
options: Real, usable numbers — like events per second and gigabytes per year — that determine which tools actually make sense
A precise financial budget for the entire project
A complete final architecture diagram
A list of every engineer needed on the team
questions.explain: A requirement like "handle NYC's taxi volume" means nothing until it's an actual number.

questions.q: Why does real estimation use round numbers and simple multiplication instead of precise figures?
options: The point is the order of magnitude, which is almost always what actually matters for a design decision — precision wastes time better spent on the design itself
Precise numbers are technically impossible to calculate in this context
Round numbers are always more accurate than precise ones
This only applies to real-time systems, not batch ones
questions.explain: A system design interview and a real decision both happen under time pressure — twenty minutes chasing precision isn't time spent designing.

questions.q: In the worked example, what did the estimated ~36.5 GB/year and 2-12 events/sec suggest about tool choice?
options: This is well within a single KQL Database's easy capacity — no sharding or unusual scale-out story required
This scale requires a fully distributed, sharded system from day one
This scale is too small for any Fabric tool to handle at all
The numbers say nothing useful about tool choice
questions.explain: The estimate immediately rules out needing specialized infrastructure built for millions of events per second.

questions.q: Why doesn't the same architecture pattern automatically scale by 100x just because it worked at a smaller size?
options: A jump from ~36.5 GB/year to 3.65 TB/year with thousands of events/sec introduces real needs — sharding, partitioning, careful capacity planning — that didn't matter before
Architecture patterns always scale linearly with no additional considerations
Scale never actually changes which tools are appropriate
This scenario is purely theoretical and never happens in practice
questions.explain: This is exactly why estimation happens before choosing storage and processing models, not after.

questions.q: What is the actual purpose of doing estimation before Lessons 4-5's storage and processing model choices?
options: To size the problem numerically first, so the tool choice is driven by real scale rather than guesswork or reflexive over-engineering
To calculate the exact dollar cost of the entire project upfront
To determine which programming language the team should use
Estimation has no real bearing on those later tool choices
questions.explain: Choosing storage or a processing model without first sizing the problem risks over-building or under-building relative to actual need.
